bull.b: Rapid revenue growth indicates broadening demand for Cloudflare’s security, performance, and developer products. Continued expansion at this scale can strengthen operating leverage, support investment in the edge network, and reinforce the company’s position as customers consolidate workloads on its platform.

A 120% net retention rate shows existing customers are materially increasing spend, while large-account growth demonstrates deeper enterprise penetration. This land-and-expand model supports recurring revenue durability, improves monetization of the installed base, and reduces reliance on constant new-customer acquisition.

Positive and improving free cash flow demonstrates that Cloudflare’s subscription model is converting growth into internally generated cash despite GAAP losses. The substantial liquid-resource base also supports continued network investment, product development, and strategic flexibility over the next several quarters.

bear.b: Leverage is high relative to the company’s still-unprofitable earnings profile, limiting financial flexibility if growth slows or funding conditions tighten. Modest cash-flow coverage of debt means more internally generated cash may need to remain dedicated to obligations rather than growth or shareholder returns.

Sustained GAAP operating and net losses show that revenue scale has not yet translated into durable bottom-line profitability. This leaves Cloudflare more dependent on continued growth and disciplined spending, while limiting the certainty of future earnings conversion if expansion becomes less favorable.

Lower gross margins indicate that network costs are growing faster than revenue, potentially constraining operating leverage as usage expands. Planned network investment of 14%–15% of revenue may support capacity and product breadth, but it can also keep cash conversion and profitability under pressure.
